around.headline: Two separate domestic-dispute deaths reported in Bengaluru in one day
around.summary: An alcoholic autorickshaw driver stabbed his wife to death and then killed himself, and in a separate case a couple was found dead at home with a family dispute suspected, per The Hindu, The Indian Express and NDTV. If you or someone you know is in an escalating domestic situation, the Women's Helpline (181) and police (100) are free and available 24x7.

around.headline: FSDA seizes over Rs 1.38 crore of expired, mislabelled food and medicine; a Bengaluru hotel shut over hygiene
around.summary: Karnataka's food safety department seized expired and mislabelled food and medicine worth more than Rs 1.38 crore from Bengaluru dark stores, and separately shut down a hotel over hygiene violations, per The Times of India and The Hindu. Worth checking expiry dates on packaged food and strips of medicine before you pay, especially from quick-commerce orders.
around.source: The Times of India, The Hindu

around.headline: Bengaluru's quiet residential lanes are turning into traffic hotspots
around.summary: Commuters rerouting around congested main roads are pushing traffic into previously quiet residential lanes across the city, per Deccan Herald. If your street has stayed calm so far, expect more through-traffic during peak hours as this rerouting spreads.

around.headline: Supreme Court declares September 11 a holiday for the BRICS Summit; November 28 to be a working Saturday instead
around.summary: The Supreme Court has declared September 11 a holiday to accommodate the BRICS Summit, with November 28 designated a working Saturday to compensate, per Live Law. Court-goers and anyone with business tied to court schedules should replan for the 11th and expect courts open on November 28.

street_smart.title: You run a small roadside stall selling Ganesh idols during festival week. Business is brisk, and every so often you have to step away — to help a customer at the back, take a phone call, or grab change — leaving the display momentarily unwatched. What's your best move to protect your stock?
street_smart.based_on: The Hindu, NDTV and The Siasat Daily, Sept 9 — a Ganesh idol was stolen from a roadside stall in Bengaluru in broad daylight, the theft caught clearly on CCTV, and police say a gang is now on their radar for targeting multiple stalls this way. This stall-theft mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: A neighbouring stall owner mentions two other vendors on the same street lost idols to quick, opportunistic thefts earlier this week — none of them had caught it on camera or reported it fast enough to matter.

choices.text: Set up even a basic phone-mounted or borrowed CCTV camera pointed at your display, keep your highest-value idols chained or behind you rather than at the open edge, and if anything goes missing, report it to the local police station immediately with the footage.
choices.feedback: Correct. This is exactly what let police act on yesterday's theft — clear CCTV footage let them identify a pattern and put a gang on their radar within a day. Cameras deter casual opportunists, keeping high-value stock out of easy reach slows down the ones who aren't deterred, and fast reporting with footage is what actually gets a case moving instead of going cold.

choices.text: Don't bother with precautions — it's a busy, well-lit street with lots of foot traffic, so nobody would risk stealing in plain sight.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Yesterday's theft happened on exactly this kind of busy street, in broad daylight — opportunistic thieves rely on the vendor's attention being split for even a few seconds, not on being unseen by the crowd. 'Busy and public' protects against some crime, but not against a quick grab-and-go when you're not looking at your own stock.

choices.text: Ask a neighbouring vendor to keep an eye on your stall while you're away, but don't mention the recent thefts to them or file anything with police since nothing's happened to you yet.
choices.feedback: Risky. An informal favour from someone equally busy with their own customers is unreliable, and staying quiet about the pattern means you can't warn each other or pool information that would help police connect the thefts to one gang. Sharing what you know, even before you're personally hit, helps everyone on the street.

choices.text: If you notice someone loitering suspiciously near your idols, immediately grab and confront them yourself before they can act.
choices.feedback: Risky. Confronting a suspected thief alone over a low-value theft can escalate into a physical altercation with no real payoff — you have no idol back yet, and you now have a conflict on your hands. Reporting the loitering to nearby police or getting camera footage of the person is far safer and still gives authorities enough to act on.

takeaways: Even a basic camera aimed at your stock is often enough — yesterday's CCTV footage from a Bengaluru stall theft let police move fast and flag a gang pattern within a day.
Keep your highest-value items chained, behind the counter, or otherwise out of easy grab-and-go reach during the busiest, most distracting hours.
Report a theft (or even suspicious loitering) to the local police station right away with any footage you have — delay is what lets a pattern go unnoticed until it's hit several vendors.

quiz.question: How much in expired and mislabelled food and medicine did Karnataka's food safety department seize from Bengaluru dark stores, per today's reports?
quiz.why: The department also separately shut down a Bengaluru hotel over hygiene violations the same day, part of a wider food-safety crackdown on the city's quick-commerce and food outlets this month.

quiz.question: The Supreme Court declared September 11 a holiday to accommodate which summit — with November 28 becoming a working Saturday to compensate?
quiz.why: Court holidays tied to major diplomatic events are common practice; litigants and lawyers need to track these compensatory working days separately from the regular court calendar.

quiz.question: Crude oil prices are climbing back toward what level a barrel amid US strikes on Iranian tankers and Iranian retaliation against Gulf shipping?
quiz.why: Oil hasn't traded near $100 a barrel in years; a sustained move to that level would likely show up in Indian pump prices within weeks, since India imports most of its crude.

quiz.question: The Strait of Hormuz, at the centre of the current US-Iran tensions, links the Persian Gulf to which body of water?
quiz.why: Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through this narrow strait, which is why any disruption there moves global crude prices so quickly.

quiz.question: Which vitamin does the human body mainly synthesise when skin is exposed to sunlight?
quiz.why: Vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium; deficiency is surprisingly common even in sunny cities like Bengaluru because most daytime hours are spent indoors or under cover.
